newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman plans to reorganise its buoyant stock market.
newsitem.headline: Oman plans to reorganise its buoyant stock market.

text.p: Oman plans to reorganise its stock exchange, the Muscat Securities Market (MSM), establishing an independent depository and settlement body and a separate regulatory function, the commerce minister said.
"Reorganisation of the market is high on the MSM's agenda," the Oman Daily Observer on Wednesday quoted Oman's Commerce and Industry Minister Makboul bin Ali bin Sultan as saying.
In a speech to the MSM's general assembly, delivered by MSM executive president Mahmoud al-Jarwani, the minister said a new law had been prepared so the market could function more professionally.
"The law provides for separation between the regulatory body and the regulated entities -- the trading floor and brokers."

Plans also included setting up a regional branch in Salalah this year, amending listing conditions to encourage foreign capital and making it obligatory for listed companies to publish unaudited quarterly financial statements.
The minister said market capitalisation rose 23 percent last year to 1.622 billion rials ($4.3 billion). Twenty-one companies were listed, one more than in 1995, and all were oversubscribed.
Trade volume climbed 130 percent, with bank and investment stocks accounting for 55 percent of the total.

Bin Sultan said primary market activity reflected business confidence, good liquidity, low interest rates on bank deposits, the saturation of investment in real estate and the relatively small value of government bonds issued last year.
Oman's stock exchange, which has over 100 stocks, has risen by over 60 percent so far this year. It is the Gulf's most open bourse and financial analysts say it is one of the region's best regulated.
